rules.text: If the query image contains complex textures (e.g., metallic strands, speckled surfaces) and Branch B cites 'discoloration', 'oxidation', or 'dirt' as the anomaly, trust A (Agent) to distinguish these from normal manufacturing variations.

If Branch B claims a 'missing logo' or 'missing text' on a capsule or similar object, trust A (Agent) to verify if the text is actually present but obscured by lighting or angle, or if the object variant legitimately lacks the text.
If Branch B's rationale focuses on subtle color shifts in metallic components (like copper strands) while Branch A explicitly notes consistency with reference strand arrangements, trust A (Agent).

If the query image shows a distinct geometric object with sharp edges (e.g., a metal part) and Branch B identifies a specific 'breakage', 'chip', or 'deformation' at a protrusion or corner, trust B (Direct).

If the anomaly is a clear structural discontinuity (like a missing tip or jagged edge) that contradicts the smooth geometry of the reference, trust B (Direct) over A's general 'consistent texture' assessment.
Exactly one single hazelnut object is present in the image.
The object shell is predominantly reddish-brown with a distinct dark brown/black base.
The shell surface exhibits a fine, longitudinal grain pattern running along the length of the nut.
The object has a continuous, smooth, convex boundary with no visible cracks or breaks.
A dark, textured circular base (hilum) is located at one end of the nut.
Surface exhibits a continuous, vertically oriented wood grain pattern with natural striations.
Surface color is restricted to a monochromatic palette of brown, tan, and amber tones.
The surface is a continuous, flat plane with no visible gaps, seams, or distinct object boundaries.
The object consists of a central dark circular aperture surrounded by concentric glass rings.
The object exhibits radial symmetry around the central axis.
The dominant colors are dark brown/black for the glass and white for the background.
The bottle opening is centered within the image frame.
Exactly three distinct insulated conductors are present within the central cross-section.
The three conductors are arranged in a tight triangular cluster, touching each other.
The three conductors must have distinct insulation colors: one green, one blue, and one brown/grey.
Each conductor core consists of a central bundle of metallic strands surrounded by a solid insulation layer.
The entire assembly is enclosed within a continuous, circular outer sheath.
Surface is uniformly brown with no other colors present.
Surface exhibits a continuous, irregular, fine-grained pebbled pattern.
Surface is continuous and free of holes, tears, or distinct foreign objects.
Surface exhibits a uniform, repeating woven grid pattern of interlaced fibers.
The surface is monochromatic, consisting exclusively of varying shades of grey.
The weave structure is continuous and intact across the entire field of view.
Exactly one screw object is present in the image.
The screw consists of a continuous shaft with a threaded section and a smooth shank.
The screw head is a flat, circular disc with a central drive recess.
The screw tip is pointed and conical.
The screw surface exhibits a metallic, slightly grainy texture.
The object is monochromatic (grayscale) with a uniform mid-tone gray.
The brush head contains exactly 36 bristle tufts arranged in a grid.
Bristle tufts are arranged in a regular 4-column by 9-row grid pattern.
The brush head has a smooth, continuous, elongated oval shape with rounded ends.
The arrangement of bristle tufts exhibits bilateral symmetry along the vertical axis.
The object consists of exactly one central circular hole surrounded by a single continuous body.
The object has exactly four protruding lobes extending radially from the central body.
The object exhibits 4-fold rotational symmetry (90-degree periodicity) in its overall geometry.
The object surface is metallic silver/grey with a slight greenish tint, set against a black background.
The surface exhibits a fine, granular metallic texture with concentric machining marks.
The central hole is perfectly circular and concentric with the outer boundary of the object.
Exactly one black rectangular component body is present in the center of the image.
Exactly three metallic legs extend downwards from the component body.
The three legs are arranged symmetrically with one central leg and two outer legs.
The component is mounted on a PCB with a grid of circular holes and vertical copper traces.
The component body features a circular indentation or marking on its top surface.
The component body is black, the legs are silver/metallic, and the PCB is copper/brown.
Surface consists exclusively of a light grey/white background with dark grey/black speckles.
Surface exhibits a dense, random distribution of irregular dark spots (speckles) across the entire field.
The surface is continuous and flat with no visible edges, seams, or distinct object boundaries.
A single vertical zipper track is centered horizontally, flanked by fabric on both sides.
The zipper teeth form a continuous, unbroken vertical chain with uniform interlocking geometry.
The fabric on both sides of the zipper exhibits a consistent, fine woven grid pattern.
The entire object (zipper and fabric) is monochromatic black or dark grey.
Surface exhibits a continuous, repeating mesh pattern of interlocking diamond-shaped apertures.
The mesh structure consists of continuous, unbroken dark lines forming the grid boundaries.
The image is monochromatic, consisting strictly of grayscale tones.
The mesh pattern covers the entire field of view uniformly without distinct foreground objects.
The object is a single, solid, oval-shaped tablet with smooth, continuous boundaries.
Two identical embossed capital letters 'F' are centered horizontally on the tablet surface.
The tablet surface is predominantly white with scattered reddish-brown speckles.
The surface texture is matte and granular, lacking gloss or smooth plastic-like reflection.
The object is a single capsule with a continuous, smooth, cylindrical body and rounded ends.
The capsule is divided into two distinct, equal-length color segments meeting at a straight vertical seam.
The capsule consists of a black segment and an orange segment.
The white text '500' is located on the orange segment.
The capsule surface is smooth and glossy, reflecting light.
Do not flag the rough, fibrous texture of the cap (hilum) or its jagged edge as a defect.
Flag circular, semi-transparent light spots or 'ghost' marks on wood grain as anomalies, even if they appear faint or lack sharp edges.
Flag rim chips or cracks even if they appear as small, localized bright reflections or irregularities on the edge.
Do not flag bright, metallic specular highlights on copper strands as defects.
Flag thin, linear foreign fibers or scratches that contrast with the woven texture, even if small.
Do not flag natural metal grain texture or slight surface unevenness on the shank as a defect.
Do not flag minor asymmetry or roughness in the drive slot of the screw head as a defect.
Flag as anomaly if bristles are splayed, bent, or disheveled, deviating from the uniform, upright alignment of the reference set.
Flag items with localized edge chipping or irregularities on the outer perimeter of the cross-arms.
Do not flag consistent, fine-grained surface texture or machining marks on the arms as defects.
Flag distinct translucent or semi-transparent shards/fragments resting on the surface, even if they appear ghostly or low-contrast against the background.
Flag dark, localized stains or discolorations on the fabric adjacent to the zipper teeth as defects.
Flag thin, dark linear intrusions that cross the mesh pattern diagonally, even if they are subtle or blend with the background texture.
Do not flag global variations in mesh orientation, density, or lighting gradients if the underlying expanded metal structure remains consistent with reference patterns.
Do not flag scattered red speckles on white tablets as defects if the 'FF' imprint is clear and the tablet shape is intact.
Flag as anomaly if the black capsule half shows surface unevenness, texture variation, or coating defects compared to the smooth orange half.
Do not flag as anomaly if the 'actavis' logo is present on the black half, even if the text appears slightly faint or low-contrast.
